tasks.registered_metrics_text:
a) Define the metric(s) to assess a property of an algorithm. These metrics should reflect the desired algorithm
properties described in assessment aim(s) (see above). State which metric(s) were used to compute the ranking(s) (if
any).
  • Example 1: Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC)
  • Example 2: Area under curve (AUC)
Gestational age at birth in weeks:
1) Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of predict to real GA at birth
2) Correlation between real and predicted GA at birth.

b) Justify why the metric(s) was/were chosen, preferably with reference to the biomedical application.

Correlation between real and predicted GA at birth does not penalise calibration issues (errors-in-variables) that
could be corrected by simple linear correction of the predictions. Mean absolute error gives the practical accuracy
in weeks.

tasks.registered_ranking_text:
a) Describe the method used to compute a performance rank for all submitted algorithms based on the generated
metric results on the test cases. Typically the text will describe how results obtained per case and metric are aggregated
to arrive at a final score/ranking.

Team rankings are computed using the mean absolute error over the test data. The team's rank is determined
using the average metric value over 1000 bootstrap samples of the test data.

b) Describe the method(s) used to manage submissions with missing results on test cases.

Scores are taken from held out data. We will calculate measures using python scripts. If the submission doesn't
include an output we request (e.g. age at birth), they are rejected. Evaluation code will be available prior to
submission so teams can test first.

c) Justify why the described ranking scheme(s) was/were used.

Bootstrapping provides an estimate (with CI) of the true ranking of a team / algorithm. The metrics themselves
have been selected to robustly assess the performance of the challenge.

tasks.registered_metrics_text:
a) Define the metric(s) to assess a property of an algorithm. These metrics should reflect the desired algorithm
properties described in assessment aim(s) (see above). State which metric(s) were used to compute the ranking(s) (if
any).
  • Example 1: Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC)
  • Example 2: Area under curve (AUC)
Reported metrics for the lesion segmentation:
1) Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) between manual and calculated lesions (binarised at 50% when the output is
probabilistic).
2) 6 metrics defined in Carass Sci Rep 10, 8242 (2020): 1-1: Correct Detection, 1-N: Merge, M-1: Split, M-N: Split-
Merge, 0-1: Detection Failure, 1-0: False Alarm
3) MAE of lesion volume in each ROI defined by DrawEM (dHCP structural pipeline), averaged within each case
4) global DSC in each DrawEM ROI, averaged
5) If non-binary / fuzzy segmentations are provided: area under the Precision-Recall curve (AUPRC)

b) Justify why the metric(s) was/were chosen, preferably with reference to the biomedical application.



 Baby Steps

1) Dice score is a robust metric for ranking algorithms but does not take lesion volume into account.
2) The 6 metrics defined in Carass et al are a complete taxonometry useful to evaluate lesions consisting of none or
multiple instances per case.
3) Total lesion volume in specific anatomical regions is likely a good predictor of clinical outcome.
4) In addition to total lesion volume, location and shape are assessed using DSC in each ROI.
5)AUPRC is appropriate when there is a substantial class imbalance and the segmentations are fuzzy. In the context
of neonatal brain injury, typically the majority of the brain is healthy tissue so there may only be 1% of the image
that is abnormal.
tasks.registered_ranking_text:
a) Describe the method used to compute a performance rank for all submitted algorithms based on the generated
metric results on the test cases. Typically the text will describe how results obtained per case and metric are aggregated
to arrive at a final score/ranking.

Average ranks are computed across test samples and metrics: average_rank = 1/2 * (rank(global DSC) + rank(MAE
of lesion volume in each DrawEM ROI, averaged)). Team rankings are computed using the average rank calculated
from 1000 bootstrap samples of the test data.

b) Describe the method(s) used to manage submissions with missing results on test cases.

Scores are taken from held out data. We will calculate measures using python scripts. If the submission doesn't
include an output we request (in this case an estimate of lesions), they are rejected. Evaluation code will be
available prior to submission so teams can test first.

c) Justify why the described ranking scheme(s) was/were used.

Bootstrapping provides an estimate (with CI) of the true ranking of a team / algorithm. The metrics themselves
have been selected to robustly assess the performance of the challenge.
